summary: Quote latency degradation was not caused by pricing-engine. At 13:22:10 the redis-cache primary node (redis-cache-2) failed health checks (3 consecutive PING timeouts) and was marked down; at 13:22:52 failover promoted replica redis-cache-3, whose dataset was empty because it was still resyncing. This wiped the shared cache (hit ratio 96%→16.8%, memory 70%→9.9%, no evictions). market-data-service, which prices quotes out of redis-cache, entered a "cache miss storm", rebuilding each quote from the exchange feed snapshot (2–8s), which raised its p99 from ~40ms to ~1790ms and CPU from ~45% to ~87%. pricing-engine, which calls market-data-service synchronously, then hit "quote computation deadline exceeded", making quotes take 2-3s on trading screens. There were zero deployments and zero config changes across all services, ruling out bad_deployment/config_change. Root cause is an infrastructure failure of the redis-cache primary plus promotion of an unsynced (empty) replica.

ranked_hypotheses.title: redis-cache primary failure promoted an unsynced empty replica, wiping the shared quote cache (infrastructure_failure)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: At 13:22:10 the redis-cache primary node redis-cache-2 failed health checks and was marked down; at 13:22:52 failover promoted replica redis-cache-3, whose dataset was empty (still resyncing). This emptied the shared quote cache (hit ratio 96%->16.8%, memory 70%->9.9%). market-data-service then rebuilt every quote from the exchange feed snapshot (2-8s per miss), raising its latency/CPU/error_rate; pricing-engine's synchronous calls to market-data-service hit deadline-exceeded, producing 2-3s quote loads.

causal_chain.claim: redis-cache-2 primary fails health check, marked down
failover promotes redis-cache-3 with empty dataset (was resyncing)
shared cache wiped: hit_ratio 96%->16.8%, memory 70%->9.9%, no evictions
market-data-service cache-miss storm rebuilds quotes from exchange feed (2-8s)
pricing-engine deadline-exceeded on market-data-service -> 2-3s quote loads

assumptions: The redis-cache node failure was not itself triggered by an upstream config/deploy change (none observed).
market-data-service has no local fallback for cache misses other than rebuilding from the exchange feed.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Pricing-engine computes every quote from scratch (code/logic regression) (rejected)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A release or logic regression in pricing-engine made quote computation slow. Rejected: no pricing-engine deployment exists (F12), pricing-engine p50 stayed ~200-330ms in its own INFO logs, and its ERRORs explicitly attribute the delay to market-data-service, not itself.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: No deployments or config changes for any service (F12, F13); pricing-engine's own errors blame market-data-service latency (F2).

ranked_hypotheses.title: exchange-gateway / external feed degradation slowed quote rebuilds (rejected)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The exchange feed became slow, so quote rebuilds took 2-8s. Rejected: exchange-gateway p99 stayed flat at ~130ms across the whole window (F11); also its only WARN was a benign 38ms NTP clock-drift message at 13:19:38. The rebuild slowness is explained by cache misses forcing the rebuild path, not by a slow feed.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: exchange-gateway latency unchanged (F11); no upstream error/latency anomaly.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Redis memory-exhaustion/eviction pressure (rejected)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: Redis ran out of memory or evicted keys, causing misses. Rejected: evictions_per_min stayed ~3/min, redis cpu ~22%, and memory FELL from 70% to 9.9% at onset (the dataset shrank, it was not over-filled). The miss cause is an empty promoted replica, not eviction.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Evictions flat (F7) and memory dropped rather than saturated (F6).

facts.statement: pricing-engine p99 jumped from ~60ms to avg 1216ms at 13:15 and 2097ms at 13:30.
pricing-engine emitted 72 'quote computation deadline exceeded: market-data-service took <n>ms' errors (max 8456ms) starting 13:23:57.
redis-cache-2 primary failed health check (3 PING timeouts) at 13:22:10 and failover promoted an empty replica redis-cache-3 at 13:22:52.
redis-cache hit_ratio fell from ~96% to 16.79% and memory from ~70% to 9.9% at 13:30, while evictions (~3/min) and CPU (~22%) stayed flat.
market-data-service logged 204 cache-miss-storm warnings (rebuilds up to 8748ms) starting 13:22:25; p99 rose 40ms->1791ms and CPU 45%->87.5% at 13:30 with flat request_rate and 0 restarts.
No deployments and no config/feature-flag changes across all services in the incident window.
Past incident HIST-107 (2025-12-09) was a cold cache storm after a redis failover that promoted an empty replica.

assumptions: No upstream deploy/config change triggered the redis node failure (none observed in deployment or config-change data).
market-data-service has no cheaper fallback than rebuilding a quote from the exchange feed on a cache miss.
The redis-cache cluster is the shared cache used by both market-data-service and pricing-engine per the dependency graph.

timeline.event: pricing-engine p99 rises from ~60ms to avg 1216ms
redis-cache-2 primary fails health check (3 PING timeouts), marked down
failover promotes replica redis-cache-3 with empty dataset
pricing-engine begins deadline-exceeded errors against market-data-service
redis hit_ratio 16.79%, memory 9.9%; market-data-service p99 1791ms, cpu 87.5%, error_rate 3.2%
redis client reconnect storm (15048 new connections in 10s)
pricing-engine p99 still elevated at avg 1191ms; recovery ongoing

recommended_actions.action: Warm/rebuild the redis-cache quote keyspace and verify replica sync is healthy before relying on it
recommended_actions.rationale: The promoted primary has an empty dataset; misses force expensive rebuilds. Restoring the cache will remove the cache miss storm.

recommended_actions.action: Add a guard so failover never promotes an unsynced/empty replica (block promotion if replica offset lags), and health-check PING timeouts trigger alerts
recommended_actions.rationale: The fault origin is promoting a resyncing empty replica; HIST-107 had the same cause.

recommended_actions.action: Add a local negative-cache/rate-limit or fallback for market-data-service quote rebuilds so a cold cache cannot stampede the exchange feed
recommended_actions.rationale: Each cache miss triggers a 2-8s synchronous rebuild; bounding this protects pricing-engine SLAs.

recommended_actions.action: Raise alerting on redis-cache hit_ratio_pct and memory_pct drops so a wiped cache is caught before downstream deadline-exceeded errors
recommended_actions.rationale: hit_ratio fell from 96% to 16.8% and memory 70% to 9.9% but was only noticed via pricing-engine symptoms.

data_gaps: Root cause of the redis-cache-2 primary health-check failure (node/infra event) is not directly observable from the available telemetry - only the downstream failure is.
redis-cache exposes no 'restarts' metric, so we cannot confirm whether the primary node crashed vs. was network-partitioned.

The all-services deployment list returned partial=true on first query; it was re-run (tc-026) and came back complete with 0 deployments, so deployment absence is confirmed for the window queried (06:00-15:00).
order-service (also a redis-cache/pricing-engine consumer) was not individually checked for impact.

findings.statement: redis-cache hit_ratio_pct collapsed from ~96% to 16.79% at 13:30 (max 97.11 at 13:15 bucket).
redis-cache memory_pct dropped from ~70% to 9.9% at 13:30, indicating the dataset was emptied (not filled).
redis-cache evictions_per_min stayed flat at ~3/min across the incident and redis cpu_pct stayed ~22%; neither eviction pressure nor redis CPU explains the hit-ratio collapse.
market-data-service logged 204 WARN 'cache miss storm: quote:<n> not in redis-cache, rebuilding from exchange feed snapshot (<n>ms)' entries starting 13:22:25, with rebuilds up to 8748ms.

findings.statement: market-data-service p99 rose from ~40ms to avg 1791ms at 13:30 and CPU from ~45% to avg 87.5%, while its request_rate stayed flat at ~950 req/s.
market-data-service error_rate rose from ~0.2% to ~3.2% at 13:30 while its pod restarts stayed at 0 (no crash/restart).
exchange-gateway p99 latency stayed flat at ~130ms throughout the incident window, so the exchange feed itself was not slow.
No deployments occurred for pricing-engine, market-data-service, redis-cache, or any service in the 06:00-15:00 window.
No configuration or feature-flag changes occurred for any service in the 04-08 to 04-09 window.

Historical incident HIST-107 (2025-12-09) matches: 'Cold cache storm after redis failover' - root cause 'Redis primary failure promoted an empty replica', services redis-cache and market-data-service.

findings.statement: Dependency graph confirms pricing-engine calls market-data-service (http) and both share redis-cache; market-data-service calls exchange-gateway (http).

Inference: The empty-replica promotion wiped the shared quote cache, and market-data-service's forced per-request rebuilds from the exchange feed (2-8s) are the proximate cause of the downstream 2-3s quote loads; pricing-engine is only the symptom holder.
